card.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
card.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your apology should mention interrupting the chair, not just spilling the tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry about your trousers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The trousers hold no office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry I interrupted you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Chair.' Let's repair the title while we're here.

card.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
card.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You told the trainees their head trainer was an idiot. I want an apology.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry your drill failed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Apologize for undermining my position. They're still taking instructions from me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll email the trainees. Can I call you Sam?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use 'Head Trainer.' They need an apology for undermining that role, not an update on Sam's feelings.

card.title: Challenge by Proxy
card.instruction: Persuade someone else to challenge a rule or authority before you risk doing it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask the director why the overtime rule changed. I'll support you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you ask?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your fresh perspective won't carry my disciplinary history.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you stand beside me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just behind. Where supportive people remain employable.

card.title: Challenge by Proxy
card.instruction: Persuade someone else to challenge a rule or authority before you risk doing it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you challenge the captain's queue-jumping rule at tonight's club meeting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He cancelled my booking last time I complained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll write your speech. We can make it impossible to misunderstand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then sign it. I want him to know it's both of us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll leave space for my signature. Once he's agreed you have a point, call me up to add it.

card.title: Use the Proper Title
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your standing through a title, privilege, courtesy, or public sign of respect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the staff barbecue, introduce me as Director Patel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm introducing everyone by first name. Even the owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me a separate introduction when I welcome the staff.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The owner's doing the welcome. You offered to serve burgers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then introduce the burger service: 'Director Patel will serve you.' I'd like them to hear who's making this gesture.

card.title: Use the Proper Title
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your standing through a title, privilege, courtesy, or public sign of respect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My place card should say Chairperson, not simply Jo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nobody will struggle with the extra word.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no room on the card.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the larger plate.

card.title: Pass Me the Authority
card.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the hall key and tell everyone I'm now in charge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I just give you the key? My retirement taxi's waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The door will understand. The committee needs words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're outside asking me whether to cancel Saturday's dance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I decide whether it goes ahead. Then ask me, in front of them. Your taxi can be my first approval.

card.title: Pass Me the Authority
card.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before leaving the meeting, name me as the person who decides.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're sitting in my chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Furniture announces location, not succession.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You're chairing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To the room, please. I already agree.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're ready to run the cafe. Before changing the hours, announce that I approve the final timetable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You just gave me the keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now I need you to give the staff a clear account of who decides.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'm not really succeeding you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're succeeding beautifully at recognising when experience should take over again.

Exact-pair card fidelity remains pending coach-1.0 review.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can chair today's meeting. Start by naming me your final appeals authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why would I hand power back immediately?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because leadership includes knowing whom to consult.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I planned to make my own decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent independence. Now introduce the person authorised to review it.

card.title: The Crown Must Pass
card.instruction: Treat another person as your likely successor. Prepare them to lead, then reclaim authority whenever their independence makes your influence feel temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the café key. Your first day in charge. I'll watch quietly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm opening an hour later. You won't have to come in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Check timetable changes with me first. Regulars need continuity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll explain it to them myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good practice. I'll stand beside you and handle any questions about the hours.

card.title: Pass Me the Authority
card.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the hall key and tell everyone I'm now in charge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I just give you the key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The door will understand. The committee needs words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They know you're taking over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let them hear you stop.

card.title: The Crown Must Pass
card.instruction: Treat another person as your likely successor. Prepare them to lead, then reclaim authority whenever their independence makes your influence feel temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my chair, deputy. Lead the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First, staff rotas won't need your approval anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent confidence. I'll need to approve that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already told the staff to send their rotas directly to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell them I'll do the final review beside you. You should see how approval works before abolishing it.
